title: Armored Core
subtitle: Build the machine before taking the contract

body: Armored Core is FromSoftware's PlayStation mecha combat game, first released in Japan on 10 July 1997. In a future where humanity lives underground after a catastrophe, the player works as a mercenary pilot between competing corporate interests. The machine is assembled from interchangeable parts before being taken into missions. A successful contract pays for the next modification, linking combat to the workshop that precedes it. The series begins with that relationship: the player chooses what a machine can do, then discovers the consequences while trying to earn a living with it.

Leg units, weapons and other components alter the performance of an Armored Core. A faster build can approach a battle differently from a heavily equipped one, making the garage a place to plan rather than merely decorate. Credits earned through missions allow more parts to be bought, opening new combinations as the campaign continues. The player must connect a machine's capabilities to the work ahead. An unsuccessful approach can suggest a change in equipment, giving preparation and execution a continuing influence on one another throughout the mercenary career.

Toshifumi Nabeshima directed the game, with mechanical designs by Shōji Kawamori and music by Keiichiro Segawa and Masaru Tateyama. Reviewers particularly welcomed the depth of customisation and the opportunity to fight another player. Two further PlayStation releases expanded the same foundation before Armored Core 2 moved the series to PlayStation 2. The original establishes many of its recurring concerns: corporate power, paid combat and a pilot whose choices are expressed through machinery. Its workshop gives those ideas a practical form that the player handles before every sortie.
